references.text: Oholiab, son of Ahisamach from the tribe of Dan, is first mentioned here as chosen by God together with Bezalel to work on the tabernacle.
Oholiab is mentioned again alongside Bezalel, and their skills as craftsmen, artists, and weavers in blue, purple, crimson, and fine linen are confirmed.
Oholiab and Bezalel carry out the work on the sanctuary with wisdom and understanding given by the Lord.
The description of materials such as blue, purple, and crimson yarn and finely spun linen used in the tabernacle's curtains, the same materials Oholiab worked with.
The same colors and materials (blue, purple, crimson, and fine linen) were used in the ephod, showing the continuity in the craftsmanship of the tabernacle.
The curtain for the gate of the courtyard was made from the same materials: blue, purple, and crimson yarn and finely spun linen, with embroidered work.
Connects Oholiab's embroidery skills to the finished product (the belt) in the sanctuary.
Shows how Oholiab's skills were applied in the making of Aaron's holy garments.
Confirms that the specific skills mentioned in 38:23 are a direct gift from God to the craftsmen.
Shows theological continuity in the use of colors and embroidery from the tabernacle to Solomon's temple.
Creates a theological parallel between Oholiab (Israel) and Hiram (Tyre), both receiving divine wisdom to build God's house.
